rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five line sensors spaced 8 mm apart across x = -16..+16 mm, placed 40 mm ahead of the axle so the robot sees the line before it reaches the wheels. The 12 mm footprint covers the 25 mm tape with overlap, so at least one sensor reads strongly at all times. Sensor weights are linear in lateral position (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1) so the signal is a smooth, proportional estimate of the line offset. Controller: base_speed 1.8 (near full PWM, to meet the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in under 3 s); kp 4 gives a full-scale steering correction of about 1400 PWM counts at signal 1, which is strong enough to track the bends without saturating; ki 0.1 removes slow bias from the motor mismatch; kd 0.1 damps oscillation. line_loss 'last_direction' keeps the robot turning toward the side it last saw the tape. Wheel radius 0.035 m and track 0.12 m are mid-range for speed and turning stability. Expected result: finishes the oval and s-bend with a low rms error. If the robot oscillates, reduce kp or raise kd. If it runs wide on sharp bends or slalom, raise kp. If it is too slow to finish, raise base_speed or wheel_radius. The measurements requested below will show which of these holds.
